<sub><sup>(message by IssueLinks)</sup></sub>
What do you mean by certain device trackers?
Trying it out on dev and it seems to work as expected
Can you share logs when this occur?

I have a similar issue.

Example:
Enabling a device_tracker will disable the POE switches that are enabled.
Enabling the POE switch (that was just disabled) will disable the device_trackers.
It seems I can't have both a POE switch and device_tracker enabled at the same time.

Further investigation:  It seems I can only enable / disable a set at once.  Anything that is enabled will be disabled when enabling or disabling another device (POE or device_tracker) or group of devices.  Vice versa happens when disabling devices as well.

> Trying it out on dev and it seems to work as expected



> What do you mean by certain device trackers?

Certain wireless devices are tracked and trying to disable them works, then within a few seconds they are re-enabled.

@Kane610 Now running 0.110.b0 and this issue appears to be resolved... thanks for your help
@grantclem awesome! Thanks for the feedback
Spoke to soon, it appears to re-populate after an update or reboot.
So do they become enabled directly after a reboot or does it happen to entities you disable after a reboot? Is it the same behaviour for all UniFi entities?

Hi, yes 30 something devices that I disable (because I enable wired devices and just leave the ones I want to track enabled), re-enable themselves after a HA restart or reboot of course.

No they stay disabled until a reboot or service restart only, unlike before.
disabled all, restarted HA and all re-enabled again automatically
Great, thanks for clarifying
I think I fixed it

Hi, thanks for the fix, it appears to have worked. So you know, I now have approx 7 devices enabled now, but it will still show 30 something in the integrations list

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/30598978/82389863-cbd4f500-9a6f-11ea-8657-9682446b2857.png)
